RecordSync.target.cfg.ref: I5, I12 and the snapshot and fence properties over a reliable reply channel: 3 writes, 2 foreign writes, 2 repeated change events, 1 forced read

RecordSync.target-lost-reply.cfg.ref: The same properties when one write reply is lost and the write may land at any later step: 3 writes, 3 edits, 2 foreign writes, 2 repeated change events

RecordSync.liveness-flush.cfg.ref: EditEventuallySettled and EventuallyCurrent under weak fairness of the store, the authority and the watch; one reply may be lost, and the lost write need not land. A bounded claim: two edits, one foreign write and one lost reply need at most 5 writes, and the same configuration violates EditEventuallySettled at 4 writes, or with a second foreign write, by exhausting MaxWrites, so a liveness failure after widening a bound is first a bound artefact

RecordSync.today-slots.cfg.ref: The entries and layout stores today, and the view store before taucad/tau#1602: a watch read that starts after the write reply supersedes the refresh read and finds the in-flight set empty, so the store publishes its own bytes as foreign
RecordSync.today-slots.cfg.fixedBy: graphics-event-driven-state-charter G2 (the entries and layout stores); taucad/tau#1602 fixed the view store

RecordSync.today-slots-ForeignStaysForei.ref: The two-slot stores keep I12, also with one lost reply and one forced read

RecordSync.post-1602-slots.cfg.ref: Handoff review R17: over a reliable reply channel, with no forced read and with one write in flight at a time, the three-slot view store has no OwnWriteAttributed counterexample at 3 writes, 2 foreign writes and 2 repeated change events; the pass rests on publish returning early for bytes already shown

RecordSync.post-1602-lost-reply.cfg.ref: Handoff review R17: the three-slot view store forgets a write whose reply was lost once the read-back returns, even when a watch read superseded that read-back; the watch read then publishes the lost write's bytes as foreign

RecordSync.post-1602-forced-read.cfg.ref: Handoff review R17: a forced read (retryRead, or the first read after a failed one) publishes even when its bytes are already shown; after the reply of a write no read overlapped, no slot holds the write, so the forced read publishes the store's own bytes as foreign

RecordSync.post-1602-ForeignStaysForeign.ref: The three-slot view store: a change event supersedes the refresh read of an overlapped write, so the acknowledged slot stays; the reply of the next write, which no read overlapped, publishes it and leaves the slot, and one foreign write of the earlier write's bytes is then attributed own

RecordSync.post-1602-SnapshotMonotone.cf.ref: As built, a read that started before a write was issued can publish a newer foreign version while the write is in flight; the reply then publishes the older own version over it until the next read

RecordSync.no-digest.cfg.ref: Attribution none: without the map a watch read of the store's own bytes is foreign

RecordSync.issued-before-read.cfg.ref: DropOnRead issued-before-read: a read that returns the base bytes drops the entry of a write still in flight, so its echo is foreign

RecordSync.drop-on-foreign-only.cfg.ref: DropOnRead foreign-only: a read attributed to the write in flight leaves an older acknowledged entry, which then claims a foreign write of its bytes

RecordSync.foreign-identical-bytes.cfg.ref: DropOnRead never: after the store read a foreign version, a foreign write of bytes identical to an old own write is attributed own

RecordSync.keep-earlier-acknowledged.cfg.ref: DropOnAck off: an entry that a later own write replaced claims a foreign write of its bytes

RecordSync.digest-keyed-entries.cfg.ref: EntryKey digest: a write lands and its reply is lost, the retry of the same bytes conflicts and removes the entry of both, and the conflict read publishes the store's own bytes as foreign

RecordSync.publish-on-overlap.cfg.ref: ReplyPublish always: the reply of an overlapped write publishes its version over a newer foreign version a read already published

RecordSync.overlap-on-start-only.cfg.ref: OverlapOnComplete off: a read that started before the write was issued and completes while it is in flight publishes a newer foreign version, and the reply then publishes the older own version over it

RecordSync.no-refresh.cfg.ref: Refresh off: an overlapped write is never published and no read follows, so the snapshot stays behind the file

RecordSync.no-wait-latest-read.cfg.ref: WaitLatestRead off: a watch read that supersedes the conflict or refresh read frees the writer, which issues its next write on a base it already knows is stale; that write conflicts with the write bound then spent, so the second edit is never written

RecordSync.no-fence.cfg.ref: Fence off: a pending edit is written after the view closed
